transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-08 14:30 PDT | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Sanjay (Lyra CTO), Aisha (Lyra ML), Tom (Lyra Platform), Nina (Lyra PM)

Summary: POC scoping for Lyra Insurance to validate Redwood inference for claims triage and customer response generation. Focus areas: success criteria (latency/cost/quality), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and integration approach (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs, tool/function calling, structured JSON output).

Topics: success criteria, throughput and concurrency sizing, benchmark methodology, private vs dedicated deployment, SDK integration, function/tool calling, structured outputs and validation, security & compliance checklist, timeline and next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate you carving out time. Quick intros?
00:12 Sanjay (Lyra): Sanjay here, CTO, gonna be owning the outcome. Aisha will run the ML side.
00:18 Aisha: Hi all, excited to dig in, we want to make sure latency and hallucination rates meet our compliance bar.
00:25 Luis (Redwood SE): Luis from Redwood, I’ll run the benchmarks and help with integration details.
00:30 Nina (PM): Nina, product owner for claims automation.
00:36 Tom: Tom on infra, I’ll handle network/VPC questions.
00:45 Maya: Great. Goal for today: agree success criteria and technical scope for a 4-week POC with a 2-week benchmark run.

02:10 Speaker 2 (Sanjay): High level our success metrics are: 1) p95 latency under 250ms for 256-token responses (lower is better), 2) response accuracy/hallucination tolerance: <5% critical errors on our golden set, 3) cost target below current in-house transformer infra by 20% on per-token basis, and 4) data residency and audit logs must be preserved.

04:05 Luis: Quick flag - p95 numbers depend on model choice and deployment: hosted API can hit lower latency for small payloads but dedicated gives more predictable throughput under load. We should plan benchmark variants: hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated reserved pool, and Private VPC (if you need on-prem).

05:30 Aisha: For workload sizing, our initial estimate is 1,200 concurrent sessions at peak, average prompt+response ~ 350 tokens, estimated 45M tokens/month. That was from our analytics. Does that map to dedicated sizing?

06:02 Luis: Yes, that helps. For 45M tokens/month with 1,200 concurrency, we’ll propose a dedicated pool spec (N GPUs) and a hosted fallback. We’ll model batching efficiency and prefix cache; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching profiles. For the POC we'll test model variants: redwood-v2-base, redwood-v2-medium-quant4 and a smaller quantized candidate for cost checks.

08:12 Tom: Network - we need to know if Redwood can support VPC peering and private endpoints. Also TLS and bring-your-own-KMS for encryption at rest.

08:45 Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering, private control plane, and KMS/HSM integrations. For the POC we can start with Dedicated with secure peering; if you require air-gapped, we can discuss Private deployment but that pushes timeline.

10:05 Sanjay: Timeline question — we are Q3 rollout target, need POC done by end of May to decide. Can Redwood deliver an end-to-end POC in ~3 weeks?

10:30 Luis: Realistically the bench and integration can be done in two phases: Phase A (1 week) - baseline hosted tests and integration via OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs; Phase B (1-2 weeks) - dedicated capacity benchmark, stress tests, and quality evals. So 3 weeks is feasible if we get artifacts and access quickly.

12:00 Aisha: Integration detail — we prefer minimal code changes. Can Redwood offer an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so our existing code (openai.Node/Python calls) works? Also function/tool-calling — we need structured JSON for downstream systems and deterministic schemas.

13:25 Luis: Yes, Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible endpoints plus official SDKs (Python, Node). Function calling is supported; we can return structured JSON via function spec schemas and also a forced-json output mode. Note: function calling can be streamed or non-streamed; streaming JSON requires a validation step.

15:00 Nina: On validation — we need auto-validators for schema conformance and a regression alerting on quality metrics. Does Redwood offer built-in structured-output validation?

15:28 Maya: Redwood Console includes basic evals and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; for the POC Luis can wire up a simple validator pipeline (match payload against JSON schema + sample accuracy checks) and expose regression alerts. Full production will integrate your CI.

17:10 Aisha: About benchmarks — what does Redwood need from us?

17:25 Luis: We need: 1) golden prompt set (50-200 examples) with expected outputs, 2) traffic profile (concurrency over time, average tokens), 3) representative sample logs, and 4) network egress constraints. We'll run latency p50/p95, token throughput, cost per token, and hallucination rate against your golden set.

18:40 Sanjay: Can you run tests that measure cold-starts, KV cache hit patterns, and multi-tenant interference? Those are big for us.

19:05 Luis: We'll design the benchmark to include cold-start samplings, sustained runs to warm caches, and interference tests with mixed workloads. We'll capture KV cache hit ratios and report tail latency. We'll also show model fallback behavior under capacity limits.

21:30 Tom: Regarding tooling — will we get SDK-based examples for function calling + typed responses? Our stack uses TypeScript + Koa microservices.

21:52 Luis: We'll share a repo with TypeScript examples, Node SDK snippets, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint sample that replicates function calling. We'll include a small middleware for JSON-schema validation.

24:10 Aisha: Data retention and logs — can we keep all request/response logs in our account for audit? And is there redaction support for PHI?

24:40 Maya: Yes, you can configure retention settings; Redwood Private/Dedicated options allow customer-controlled logs. We also support configurable request redaction and integration with customer KMS for encryption. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 docs.

26:00 Nina: Pricing — we need a cost model for hosted vs dedicated + pilot credits. Is there a templated POC SOW?

26:20 Maya: We'll send a POC SOW with pricing for a 4-week pilot, options for dedicated reserved capacity, and an estimate of expected unit cost at your projected volume. We'll include assumptions about tokens, concurrency, and any egress costs.

28:55 Aisha: On model quality — we may require fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge of policy documents. Does Redwood support retrieval or external tool calling?

29:20 Luis: Support for tool calling/LLM-as-a-service to external retrieval is possible; we can integrate with your vector DB via a lightweight retriever or you can call out to an external retriever and pass the context. For POC we usually simulate retrieval with a small in-memory store.

31:40 Sanjay: Any concerns about vendor lock-in? We want an approach where we can switch endpoints with minimal code changes.

32:00 Maya: OpenAI-compatible endpoints and standard SDKs help with portability. We'll document the differences and provide a compatibility checklist. Dedicated configs are portable across regions but custom infra (on-prem) will require more integration work.

34:10 Tom: For the dedicated test, what telemetry will we get? Token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, error traces?

34:35 Luis: Yes - Redwood Console will surface token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. For the POC we'll grant a project-level view and logs.

36:50 Nina: Any regulatory constraints we should be aware of before POC? E.g., storing PII in logs, residency.

37:05 Maya: We'll map that in the security docs. If you need data never to leave EU/US regions, we can place dedicated capacity in those regions. And for PII/PII redaction we can show options.

39:10 Aisha: How will we measure hallucination rate? Do you have tooling to compute falses vs ground truth?

39:35 Luis: We'll execute automated scoring against your golden set, and also run manual spot checks. We'll report precision/recall for extraction tasks and free-text hallucination rates. We'll also provide per-prompt breakdowns so we can iterate on prompts.

41:00 Maya: Ok let's recap deliverables: 1) Redwood to send SOW, security pack, and example SDK snippets; 2) Lyra to submit golden set, traffic profile, and sample logs; 3) Redwood to schedule benchmark start week of 2025-05-19; 4) follow-up technical sync 2025-05-14 to confirm network/VPC and runbook.

42:20 Sanjay: Sounds good. One more question — can you support function calling with strict JSON schema + deterministic output for claims parsing?

42:45 Luis: Yes, we'll use function spec schemas and a forced-json generation mode; we also recommend a small validation service to reject/repair outputs. We'll include an example that uses schema-first generation in TypeScript.

44:00 Tom: For the dedicated pilot, who runs the capacity — Redwood or do we provide infra?

44:20 Maya: Redwood manages Dedicated pools in our cloud tenants; for Private deployments we can deploy into your VPC or on-prem rack depending on contract. For most pilots the Dedicated option hits the balance of control and speed.

46:05 Aisha: Any gotchas on streaming vs non-streaming? We need partial results quickly for UI, but also strict schema at the end.

46:30 Luis: We can stream tokens for UX and then emit a final validated JSON payload. The streaming path can include typed delta events but final validation happens once complete. We'll provide SDK helpers for that pattern.

48:10 Nina: Are there sample dashboards for regression alerts we can see?

48:25 Luis: We'll share a demo of Redwood Console dashboards and an example alert rule tied to your golden set failing accuracy thresholds.

50:00 Maya: Great. Any final risks we should call out?

50:12 Sanjay: Main risk is timeline - if we don't get sample data quick, it's hard to meet May target. Also network approvals can take time.

50:30 Maya: Understood. We'll prioritize the SOW and security pack today and ask for your sample artifacts.

52:00 Action recap (verbal): Maya: I will send SOW/security. Luis: bench plan + scripts. Aisha/Tom: sample data & network answers. Nina: final success criteria doc.

54:00 Meeting close: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the repo, SOW, and benchmark tracking spreadsheet. Links mentioned: deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/lyra-poc), benchmark sheet (https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/lyra-sim), SDK repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-examples).

(Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors, speaker labels approximate; some technical terms abbreviated or mis-typed, e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "quant-4" instead of quant4.)
